name.description: The host name of the machine.

os.description: The name and version of the operating system.

cpuCount.description:
Returns the number of CPUs that the current process (JVM or Python Interpreter) can use, taking into account the container CPU limits and system CPUs.
In Python, this can be used instead of Python native `os.cpu_count()` which returns the number of logical CPUs in the system,
not what the container is restricted to.
Checkout {@link https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/80235} for more info.

On client Python, information is retrieved from `/sys/fs/cgroup/cpu/` which is similar to how pylint solved
the problem {@link https://github.com/d1gl3/pylint/blob/b4f5c4482e37045d75188bc3087196a70cdbe575/pylint/lint/run.py#L34}
and how OpenJDK used to solve it {@link https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/80235#issuecomment-1505024722}.

When called from client Python SDK, the number belongs to the client node (eg. JupyterLab container), not the server.

memoryGB.description: The maximum memory available to Java in GB.

osMemoryGB.description: The total memory available to the instance.

instanceType.description:
Information about the virtualization infrastructure hosting the machine.

@see https://aws.amazon.com/ec2/instance-types/

label.description:
A computed label for comparing like machines. For AWS machines, this will be
the instance type, otherwise it will be string such as "MacBookPro11,3" for MAC OS X
(or "other" if nothing else can be determined).
